subject: physics
question_text: As we go from one planet to another, how do (a) the mass and (b) the weight of a body change?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The mass
lines: The mass of a body is the quantity of matter
in it. It is the same everywhere and does not
change from one planet to another.
steps.why: Mass measures how hard a body is to accelerate, and that property travels with the body.
common_mistakes: Saying the mass becomes smaller on a smaller planet.

recall.must_convey: That the mass is the quantity of matter and does not change from planet to planet.

lines.text: Mass stays the same; weight changes.

steps.why: One number belongs to the body and the other to the body AND the planet — which is the whole distinction the question is testing.
common_mistakes: Treating weight as a property of the body alone.

recall.must_convey: That weight is m g and changes because g differs from planet to planet.
accept: g is different so weight changes
